notes:
I couldn't do this research. My search and fetch tool was blocked before it returned anything: the first batch of searches failed with a "no more tool calls remaining this turn" error, and a retry failed the same way. My other tools have no internet access, so I didn't read any pages on your approved sites.

You told me to report only what pages actually say, give a URL for every point and leave out anything I couldn't find. Since I found nothing, I have no notes to give you. Writing them from memory would break those rules and could put made-up views or links in front of lay readers.

When the tool is working again, here's what I'd do:

1. **Verse-by-verse sources (traditional reading):** Enduring Word on 2 Samuel 24, Bible Hub's commentaries on each verse (Ellicott, Pulpit Commentary, Gill, Matthew Henry, Keil & Delitzsch), StudyLight and Precept Austin.
2. **Main questions to research:**
   - **v. 1:** God "stirred up" David here, while 1 Chronicles 21:1 says Satan did. How do these fit together? This is where Reformed (God ruling over all events), Wesleyan/Arminian (God allowing it) and Lutheran writers are most likely to differ.
   - **vv. 1–10:** Why was the census a sin? Common explanations include pride or trust in military strength, and the missing half-shekel ransom of Exodus 30:12. Joab's objection (v. 3) and David's guilty conscience (v. 10) belong here too.
   - **vv. 15–17:** Why the people suffered for David's sin, and David as a shepherd who offers himself for the flock.
   - **vv. 18–25:** The threshing floor as the later Temple site (2 Chronicles 3:1), "offerings that cost me nothing" (Spurgeon and Desiring God), and the 50 shekels here versus 600 shekels in 1 Chronicles 21:25.
3. **Other views:** NET Bible notes on the textual details, Bible Odyssey on the two accounts, Catholic sources (New Advent's Haydock or Church Fathers material, Catholic.com) and Orthodox sources (OCA). I'd also check whether any site discusses "sacrificial giving" as prosperity teaching.

If you send the request again, I'll run these searches and write the notes verse by verse, with a URL after each point.
